title: Decisions, assignments, loops, collections, subflows, and transforms
objectives: Use a Decision element to branch on conditions instead of stuffing logic into a validation rule or Apex if/else by default.
Use Assignment to set variables and to add record variables to collections, including consecutive assignment rows.
Loop collections and keep DML outside the loop by building a collection, matching Help's bulkification example.
Call a subflow to remove repetition and use Transform to join collections, without treating those as formula fields or approval steps.
diagnostic_question: An after-save Flow gets Opportunity team members and must create a Task per member when the team is not empty. Before reading, where do Decision, Loop, Assignment, collection, and a single Create Records go—and why not DML inside the loop or a validation rule?
definition: Inside a Flow, Decision elements branch on conditions, Assignment elements set variables (including adding to collections), Loop elements iterate a collection, subflows run another flow to reduce repetition, and Transform can join collections. Help's bulkification example combines Decision, Loop, Assignment, and a single Create Records after the loop so DML is not inside the loop. ([Assignment Element](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.flow_ref_elements_assignment.htm); [Bulkified Record Processing](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.automate_flow_build_example_bulkified_processing.htm); [Transform Element](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.flow_ref_elements_transform.htm); [Which automation tool](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.process_which_tool.htm))
why_it_matters: Interviewers listen for 'never DML inside a loop' and for Decision versus validation versus Apex. Assignment is how you build collections; it is not a formula field. Subflow is how you reuse an autolaunched Flow, not an approval process.
sixty_second_explanation: Think of a corporate mailroom. A Decision is the routing bins (domestic vs overnight). Assignment is stamping the envelope and dropping it into a mailbag (collection). A Loop walks each envelope in the bag. Transform merges two trays of addresses into one. A subflow is sending the bag to another department's posted procedure. Validation is the inspector who refuses an illegal parcel at the dock—not a bin. A formula is the printed postage chart. Approval is a manager's signature. Apex is a custom sorting machine when the mailroom cards cannot keep up.
deeper_explanation: Assignment Element: set values in variables, including collection, record, record collection, and global variables. Specify variable, operator, and value. Multiple rows run consecutively in listed order. To update a record variable and add it to a collection, use Assignment on a Loop's For Each path, then Create Records outside the loop. Add operator adds the record variable to the collection. Fault paths can assign an error message into a variable for a Screen. ([Assignment Element](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.flow_ref_elements_assignment.htm))

Bulkified Record Processing: never perform DML inside loops; collect records during the loop, then one Create/Update/Delete after. Use a Decision to skip work when a collection is empty. Loop first-to-last through team members. Assignment builds each Task record variable, then Assignment Add to TasksToCreate. After the loop, one Create Records from the collection. This after-save example is for related Tasks, not a validation rule. ([Bulkified Record Processing](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.automate_flow_build_example_bulkified_processing.htm))

Which-tool: run another flow in the current interview to reduce repetition—Autolaunched or Screen depending on the child. Subflow input variable API names can be up to 40 characters. Disabling input on a child variable can break the parent. ([Which automation tool](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.process_which_tool.htm); [Flow Variable Considerations](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.flow_considerations_feature_variable.htm))

Transform Element Help exists to transform and join collections (for example combining external and Salesforce orders into one structure for a data table). Do not treat Transform as a formula field on the object or as Apex. Confirm current GA/beta status in the org if the picker differs. ([Transform Element](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.flow_ref_elements_transform.htm))

Decision is not a validation rule: a Decision routes the interview; a validation rule refuses a save when True. Complex screen validation may use Decision (AUTO-004). Apex if/else is complementary when CPU or volume exceeds Flow, not the default branch.

mental_model.analogy: A corporate mailroom: Decision = routing bins, Assignment = stamp plus drop into the bag, Loop = process each envelope, collection = the mailbag, Transform = merge two address trays, subflow = another department's procedure.
useful_mapping: Decision → which bin the envelope takes
Assignment Equals → stamp a field on the current envelope
Assignment Add → drop the envelope into the mailbag collection
Loop → walk the bag first item to last
Create Records after the loop → one trip to the loading dock (one DML)
subflow → send the bag to another posted procedure
Transform → reformat two trays into one
where_it_breaks: Governor limits are not a mailbag size you can see (APEX-007 / AUTO-007).
Validation happens at the dock before some of this mailroom even runs.
Transform GA/beta and join features are release-sensitive.
Apex remains the custom sorter for CPU-heavy or Batch volume work.

interview_explanation.thirty_seconds: Decision branches. Assignment stamps variables and Add drops records into a collection. Loop walks the collection. DML stays after the loop. Subflow reuses another flow. Transform joins collections. Validation is not a Decision. Apex is complementary, not the default if/else.
interview_explanation.two_minutes: I draw Help's after-save Task example: Get team members, Decision if empty, Loop, Assignment to build each Task, Assignment Add to a collection, one Create Records. I never put Create Records inside the loop. I extract repeated steps to an autolaunched subflow with input names at or under 40 characters. I use a validation rule only when the save must be refused, and Apex only for CPU or Batch volume.

terminology.plain: A branch in the interview based on conditions.
terminology.precise: Define conditions in a Decision; paths run when criteria match. Help also uses Decision to skip work when a collection is empty and for complex screen validation logic.
terminology.example: Decision: team member collection is empty → end.
terminology.non_example: Validation rule: True means illegal save, not an interview branch.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: If/else in Apex: complementary, not the default.
terminology.boundary: Wait conditions are a different element.

terminology.plain: The element that writes values into variables.
terminology.precise: Variable, operator, value; multiple rows consecutive. Add operator appends a record variable to a collection on a Loop path.
terminology.example: Set TaskRecord.Subject, then Add TaskRecord to TasksToCreate.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Update Records: DML, not in-memory assignment.

terminology.plain: Iterates a collection first-to-last or last-to-first.
terminology.precise: For Each path processes the current item. After Last is where bulk DML belongs.
terminology.example: Loop Opportunity Team Members first item to last item.
terminology.non_example: A scheduled Flow batch is not this Loop element.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Apex for-loop: similar idea, different language.
terminology.boundary: Do not put Create Records on For Each.

terminology.plain: A variable that holds multiple values or records.
terminology.precise: Record collection variables hold many Salesforce records for later DML. Assignment Add builds them in memory.

terminology.plain: An element that runs another flow in the same interview.
terminology.precise: Reduces repetition. Child is often autolaunched (no screens) when the parent is record-triggered. Input API names up to 40 characters.
terminology.example: Parent after-save calls LAB_BuildFollowUpTasks autolaunched child.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Invocable Apex: code action, not a flow.
terminology.boundary: Disabling child inputs breaks the parent.

terminology.plain: An element that maps or joins collections into a target structure.
terminology.precise: Help describes joining source collections into one target collection, for example orders from an external system plus Salesforce orders for a data table.
terminology.example: Join NetSuite and Salesforce order collections for a screen table.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Assignment Add: manual collection build, not Transform.

terminology.plain: Designing the Flow so one DML handles many records instead of DML per loop iteration.
terminology.precise: Help: never DML inside loops; collect, then one Create Records after. Design for bulk from the start because record-triggered flows can process multiple records.
terminology.example: 20 Closed Won Opportunities still create Tasks with DML after each interview's loop, not per team member inside the loop.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Apex bulkification: sibling concept in APEX-007/010.

terminology.plain: The Loop path that runs for the current collection item.
terminology.precise: Put Assignment here to stamp the current item and Add to a collection. Do not put Create Records here.
terminology.example: Build TaskRecord from Current Item from Loop.
terminology.non_example: After Last path: where Create Records goes.
terminology.boundary: Current item is not $Record unless you mapped it.

when_to_use: Use a Decision element when the Flow interview must branch, including skipping work when a collection is empty—not when a validation rule must refuse the save.
Use Assignment to set variables and to Add record variables to a collection inside a Loop.
Use a Loop plus one Create/Update/Delete after Last when many related records must be written, matching Help's bulkification example.
Use a subflow when another Flow should run in this interview to reduce repetition, with input API names at or under 40 characters.
Use Transform when you must join collections; use Apex only if CPU or Batch volume exceeds what these elements can do.
when_not_to_use: Do not put Create Records, Update Records, or Delete Records inside a Loop's For Each path.
Do not use a Decision element as a substitute for a validation rule that must block illegal data on every channel.
Do not use Assignment as a substitute for a formula field that should always calculate on the record without an interview.
Do not use a subflow as a substitute for an approval process when a person must approve.
Do not start in Apex if/else for Help's Opportunity-team Task pattern that Decision, Loop, and Assignment already cover.

interview_questions.question: Walk Decision, Assignment, Loop, and collection for Closed Won Tasks.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Get members, Decision if empty, Loop, Assignment to build each Task, Assignment Add to a collection, one Create Records after the loop.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I cite Help's bulkification example and Assignment's Add-to-collection pattern. I never put DML on For Each. I do not use a validation rule to create Tasks or Apex as the first design. After-save is the Start optimization because these are related records.
interview_questions.example: Three LAB_ team members → three Tasks, one Create Records.

interview_questions.question: Assignment versus a formula field?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Assignment writes a Flow variable during the interview, including collections. A formula field always calculates on the record without a Flow run.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: If the percent should show even when no Flow runs, that is a formula. If I am building Task records in a loop, that is Assignment. Validation is neither—it blocks saves. Apex properties are a different language (APEX-001).
interview_questions.example: TaskRecord.Subject Equals 'Follow up' versus a formula on Opportunity.
weak_answer_warnings: Using Flow Assignment as always-on calculate

interview_questions.question: CPU timeout; Create Records is inside a Loop. Fix?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Move DML after Last. Use Assignment to build a collection, then one Create Records. That is Help's refactor, not an automatic Apex rewrite.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I also add a Decision for empty collections and entry conditions. I only take Batch Apex if volume exceeds scheduled Flow, which is a different problem. I do not use a validation rule to 'reduce CPU'.
interview_questions.example: Closed Won Flow creating Tasks per member inside For Each.
follow_ups: Does after-save async path change this?

interview_questions.question: Two Flows copy the same Task-build steps. What do you extract?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: An autolaunched subflow, because which-tool says run another flow to reduce repetition. Keep input API names at or under 40 characters.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: The child cannot have screens if the parent is record-triggered in the usual pattern. I do not extract to an approval process. I do not disable inputs the parent still sets.
interview_questions.example: LAB_BuildFollowUpTasks called from two after-save parents.

interview_questions.question: When is a Decision the wrong tool?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: When illegal data must never save—that is a validation rule. When a person must approve—that is an approval. When you only need always-on calculate—that is a formula. When CPU/volume exceeds Flow—Apex.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: Decision is an interview branch, including empty-collection skips and complex screen checks. I will not hide a hard data rule in a Decision after the save.
interview_questions.example: Amount < 0 must fail Data Loader: validation, not Decision.
weak_answer_warnings: Decision as the only data-quality gate

interview_questions.question: What is Transform for in this lesson?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Joining or mapping collections into a target collection, for example mixing external and Salesforce orders for a screen table. It is not a formula field and not Apex.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I confirm the element is available in the org because Help has described it across beta/GA. If Transform is missing, Assignment Add is the manual mailbag. I still bulkify DML.
interview_questions.example: Join two LAB_ order collections for a data table.

interview_questions.question: Parent Flow cannot set the subflow input. Checks?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Child Available for Input, API name length ≤ 40, data types match, referenced flow active. Disabling input on an existing variable can break the parent.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I do not jump to Apex. I do not replace the subflow with an approval. Record collections are allowed as Flow resources even when App Builder cannot pass them.

interview_questions.question: Mailroom analogy, then break it.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Decision is bins, Assignment stamps and bags, Loop walks envelopes, Transform merges trays, subflow is another department. It breaks on governors you cannot see and on validation that happens at the dock before the mailroom.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: Formula is the postage chart, approval a manager signature, Apex a custom sorter for CPU/volume. No labeled-drawer story. DML inside the loop is sending a truck per envelope.
interview_questions.example: Create Records on For Each as the broken analogy.
